claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A transformer-based model can predict Young’s modulus for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
A transformer-based model can predict yield strength for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
A transformer-based model can predict fracture toughness for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
Integrating microstructural descriptors and electronic-structure parameters will reduce prediction RMSE by 30–50%.
The proposed model will be more than ten times faster than conventional first-principles and CALPHAD approaches.
Attention-based features can capture local ordering motifs, grain-boundary distributions, and phase heterogeneity.
Electronic-structure descriptors can represent ductility and fracture behavior in this alloy.
Learned attention weights will correlate spatial microstructural and chemical fluctuations with local stress distributions.
Learned attention weights will identify damage-initiation sites during deformation.
Transformer self-attention can capture intricate interactions among alloying elements.
Long-range pattern recognition over microstructural and electronic descriptors will capture elastic response and localized fracture mechanisms.
The proposed feature integration will reduce reliance on computationally intensive high-fidelity simulations.
First-principles and molecular-dynamics methods are too time-consuming for high-throughput alloy-structure prediction.
CALPHAD can require significant computing resources and can be limited by inadequate HEA databases.
Existing methods are particularly inaccurate at predicting fracture toughness.
The model may lose reliability for microstructures, chemical fluctuations, or processing-induced heterogeneities outside its training regime.
Transformer models have outperformed random forests and Gaussian processes for HEA elongation and ultimate tensile-strength prediction.
Attention-weight visualizations in an HEA transformer have revealed elemental relationships consistent with metallurgical principles.
The exact improvement in fracture-toughness prediction for HfNbTiVAl10 has not yet been validated.
